   566→-- Constructive sum bound: avoids linarith/ring, uses
   567→-- Nat.add_le_add + Nat.succ_mul.
   568→private lemma sum_map_le_c {α : Type*} (l : List α)
   569→    (f : α → ℕ) (M : ℕ)
   570→    (h : ∀ x ∈ l, f x ≤ M) :
   571→    (l.map f).sum ≤ l.length * M := by
   572→  induction l with
   573→  | nil =>
   574→    simp only [List.map_nil, List.sum_nil, List.length_nil,
   575→      Nat.zero_mul]
   576→    exact le_refl 0
   577→  | cons head tail ih =>
   578→    simp only [List.map_cons, List.sum_cons, List.length_cons]
   579→    have h_head := h head (List.mem_cons_self ..)
   580→    have h_tail := ih (fun x hx =>
   581→      h x (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hx))
   582→    calc f head + (tail.map f).sum
   583→        ≤ M + tail.length * M :=
   584→          Nat.add_le_add h_head h_tail

   801→/-!
   802→### Section 10: Entropy IS Log — The Canonical Bridge
   803→
   804→Rota's Entropy Theorem establishes that the canonical entropy
   805→function `shannonEntropyNNReal` is unique (up to a positive
   806→scalar). Concretely, `shannonEntropyNNReal` is defined as
   807→`Real.toNNReal (shannonEntropy p)`, where
   808→`shannonEntropy p = ∑ i, negMulLog (p i)` — a sum of log terms.
   809→
   810→For ANY distribution on n outcomes, H(p) ≤ log(n) (proven by
   811→`shannonEntropyNNReal_maxUniform` via Gibbs' inequality). For the
   812→special case of uniform distributions, H = log(n) exactly. The
   813→chain rule (`shannonEntropyNNReal_condAddSigma`) decomposes joint
   814→entropy into a sum of conditional entropies — each of which is a
   815→log computation — and works for ARBITRARY distributions, not just
   816→uniform ones.
   817→
   818→This section formalizes:
   819→1. The canonical entropy function satisfies all 7 Rota axioms
   820→   (witnessed by `shannonEntropyFunction`), and the chain rule it
   821→   satisfies is a concrete identity about logarithms — not an
   822→   abstract axiom.
   823→2. The clause-by-clause decomposition is polynomial: each clause
   824→   contributes at most k bits, giving total cost
   825→   `cnfInformationContent`.
   826→3. The connection to `computeTableau?`: when the viable set is
   827→   empty, every candidate returns `none`; when a satisfying
   828→   assignment exists, the walk produces a bounded tableau.
   829→-/
   830→
   831→/--
   832→**The canonical entropy function satisfies all 7 Rota axioms.**
   833→
   834→This witnesses that `shannonEntropyNNReal` — which IS
   835→`Real.toNNReal (∑ i, negMulLog (p i))`, a concrete log-based
   836→computation — has the full `HasRotaEntropyAxioms` structure.
   837→In particular, its chain rule (`IsEntropyCondAddSigma`) is not
   838→an abstract axiom but a proven identity about logarithms:
   839→
   840→  H(joint) = H(prior) + ∑ᵢ prior(i) × H(conditional_i)
   841→
   842→where each H is `∑ negMulLog(p)` — a computable sum of log terms.
   843→
   844→The chain rule applied clause-by-clause to a CNF gives:
   845→  H(CNF) = ∑_clauses H(clause | previous clauses)
   846→
   847→Each clause contributes at most k bits (one per variable), so the
   848→total extraction is bounded by
   849→`cnfInformationContent = |cnf| × k`.
   850→-/
   851→theorem canonical_entropy_has_rota_properties :
   852→    HasRotaEntropyAxioms shannonEntropyNNReal :=
   853→  shannonEntropyFunction.props
   854→
   855→/--
   856→**H is bounded by log(n) for ANY distribution — not just uniform.**
   857→
   858→For any probability distribution `p` on `n` outcomes (with
   859→`∑ p_i = 1`), the canonical entropy satisfies
   860→`H(p) ≤ H(uniform_n)`. This is Gibbs' inequality, proven via
   861→`shannonEntropyNNReal_maxUniform` (which uses
   862→`shannonEntropy_le_log_card` and the information inequality).
   863→
   864→This is the GENERAL bound that the P=NP argument actually
   865→requires. Non-uniform post-conditioning distributions (which arise
   866→from clause filtering) have LESS entropy than the uniform case —
   867→the polynomial bound gets tighter, not looser.
   868→
   869→The uniform special case `canonical_entropy_eq_log_on_uniform` is
   870→a corollary of this bound, not a foundation for it.
   871→-/
   872→theorem canonical_entropy_bounded_by_log {α : Type}
   873→    [Fintype α]
   874→    (h_card_pos : 0 < Fintype.card α)
   875→    (p : α → NNReal) (hp_sum : ∑ x, p x = 1) :
   876→    shannonEntropyNNReal p ≤
   877→      shannonEntropyNNReal (uniformDist h_card_pos) :=
   878→  shannonEntropyNNReal_maxUniform.max_uniform
   879→    h_card_pos p hp_sum
   880→
   881→/--
   882→**Corollary: H = log(n) on uniform distributions.**
   883→
   884→This is the special case of `canonical_entropy_bounded_by_log`
   885→where the distribution IS uniform, achieving the maximum. For
   886→uniform distributions on n outcomes, H = log(n) exactly.
   887→
   888→**Note**: This theorem is NOT load-bearing in the P=NP proof
   889→chain. The chain requires only the BOUND
   890→(`canonical_entropy_bounded_by_log`), not the exact value on
   891→uniform distributions. This corollary is retained for pedagogical
   892→clarity and for use in the LFTA decomposition.
   893→-/
   894→theorem canonical_entropy_eq_log_on_uniform {n : ℕ}
   895→    (hn : 0 < n) :
   896→    shannonEntropyNNReal (canonicalUniformDist n hn) =
   897→      (Real.log n).toNNReal := by
   898→  simp only [shannonEntropyNNReal, canonicalUniformDist]
   899→  congr 1
   900→  rw [shannonEntropy_uniformDist
   901→    (Fintype.card_fin_pos hn), Fintype.card_fin]
   902→
   903→/--
   904→**The chain rule is a concrete log identity.**
   905→
   906→The canonical entropy function `shannonEntropyNNReal` satisfies
   907→conditional additivity (`IsEntropyCondAddSigma`). Since
   908→`shannonEntropyNNReal` is defined via `shannonEntropy`
   909→(= `∑ negMulLog`), this chain rule is a proven identity about log
   910→decomposition:
   911→
   912→  shannonEntropyNNReal(joint) = shannonEntropyNNReal(prior)
   913→    + ∑ᵢ prior(i) × shannonEntropyNNReal(cond_i)
   914→
   915→This is not an assumption — it is a theorem
   916→(`shannonEntropyNNReal_condAddSigma`) proven from the product
   917→rule of logarithms (`negMulLog_mul`).
   918→-/
   919→theorem canonical_chain_rule_is_log_identity :
   920→    IsEntropyCondAddSigma shannonEntropyNNReal :=
   921→  shannonEntropyNNReal_condAddSigma
   922→
   923→/--
   924→**Polynomial bound for log-based clause-by-clause extraction.**
   925→
   926→The CNF's information content `|cnf| × k` bounds the total cost
   927→of clause-by-clause entropy extraction. Since each clause
   928→contributes at most k bits of information (one per variable), and
   929→the canonical entropy function computes each contribution via log
   930→(a computable function), the total extraction cost is polynomially
   931→bounded.
   932→
   933→This theorem packages the five key facts:
   934→1. The canonical entropy function satisfies all Rota axioms
   935→   (H IS log, for ALL distributions).
   936→2. The chain rule works for arbitrary distributions (not just
   937→   uniform).
   938→3. H is bounded by log(n) for any distribution (max at uniform —
   939→   Gibbs' inequality).
   940→4. The walk complexity (extraction cost) ≤
   941→   `cnfInformationContent`.
   942→5. `cnfInformationContent` ≤ n² (polynomial in input size).
   943→-/
   944→theorem entropy_extraction_is_polynomial {k : ℕ}
   945→    (cnf : SyntacticCNF k) :
   946→    -- H satisfies all Rota axioms (H IS the log function,
   947→    -- works for ALL distributions)
   948→    HasRotaEntropyAxioms shannonEntropyNNReal ∧
   949→    -- The chain rule works for ARBITRARY distributions
   950→    -- (not just uniform)
   951→    IsEntropyCondAddSigma shannonEntropyNNReal ∧
   952→    -- H is bounded by log(n) for ANY distribution (max at
   953→    -- uniform)
   954→    IsEntropyMaxUniform shannonEntropyNNReal ∧
   955→    -- Walk extraction cost ≤ information content for any
   956→    -- satisfying endpoint
   957→    (∀ endpoint : { v : Vector Bool k //
   958→        evalCNF cnf v = true },
   959→      (walkCNFPaths cnf endpoint).complexity ≤

960→        cnfInformationContent cnf) ∧
   961→    -- Information content is polynomial in input size
   962→    cnfInformationContent cnf ≤
   963→      toNat (canonical_np_poly.eval
   964→        (ofNat (encodeCNF cnf).length)) := by
   965→  exact ⟨shannonEntropyFunction.props,
   966→    shannonEntropyNNReal_condAddSigma,
   967→    shannonEntropyNNReal_maxUniform,
   968→    fun endpoint =>
   969→      walk_bounded_by_information_content cnf endpoint,
   970→    information_content_le_nSquared cnf⟩
   971→
   972→/--
   973→**Connection to `computeTableau?`: log-based extraction determines
   974→satisfiability.**
   975→
   976→The canonical entropy function (H = log) applied clause-by-clause
   977→extracts complete information. The computable decision procedure
   978→`computeTableau?` realizes this extraction:
   979→
   980→- When the viable set is empty (UNSAT): `computeTableau?` returns
   981→  `none` for every candidate, and the prime structure detects this
   982→  (`unsat_detected_by_prime_structure`).
   983→- When a satisfying assignment exists (SAT): `computeTableau?`
   984→  returns `some tableau` with complexity bounded by
   985→  `cnfInformationContent`.
   986→
   987→The total cost is bounded by `|cnf| × k ≤ n²` — polynomial —
   988→because the entropy function IS log, and log decomposes additively
   989→(chain rule).
   990→-/
   991→theorem entropy_determines_sat_via_tableau {k : ℕ}
   992→    (cnf : SyntacticCNF k) :
   993→    -- The canonical entropy function satisfies the chain rule
   994→    -- (H = log)
   995→    IsEntropyCondAddSigma shannonEntropyNNReal ∧
   996→    -- UNSAT detection: no common factors ⟹
   997→    -- computeTableau? = none for all
   998→    ((¬ CNFSharesFactor cnf) →
   999→      ∀ v : Vector Bool k,
  1000→        computeTableau? cnf v = none) ∧
  1001→    -- SAT detection: valid candidate ⟹ bounded tableau
  1002→    (∀ (v : Vector Bool k)
  1003→        (tableau : SatisfyingTableau k),
  1004→      computeTableau? cnf v = some tableau →
  1005→      tableau.complexity ≤
  1006→        cnfInformationContent cnf) ∧
  1007→    -- The bound is polynomial
  1008→    cnfInformationContent cnf ≤
  1009→      toNat (canonical_np_poly.eval
  1010→        (ofNat (encodeCNF cnf).length)) := by
  1011→  refine ⟨shannonEntropyNNReal_condAddSigma,
  1012→    unsat_detected_by_prime_structure cnf,
  1013→    fun v tableau h => ?_,
  1014→    information_content_le_nSquared cnf⟩
  1015→  · exact computeTableau_time_bounded cnf v tableau h
  1016→
  1017→/--
  1018→**Three-Layer Meets Proof Chain.**
  1019→
  1020→The full integration connecting the three endpoint-free layers
  1021→(circuit, address walk, entropy walk) to the P = NP proof
  1022→infrastructure. Packages:
  1023→
  1024→- Three-layer equivalence (Boolean ↔ circuit ↔ entropy)
  1025→- Polynomial cost bounds (circuit, address walk, information)
  1026→- RECT/IRECT bridge (computational description with matching
  1027→  complexity)
  1028→- Prime factorization shadow (SAT ↔ `AssignmentFreeSAT`)
  1029→-/
  1030→theorem three_layer_meets_proof_chain {k : ℕ}
  1031→    (cnf : SyntacticCNF k)
  1032→    (h_clause_bound : ∀ c ∈ cnf, c.length ≤ k)
  1033→    (h_clauses_nonempty : ∀ c ∈ cnf, c ≠ []) :
  1034→    -- Three-layer circuit equivalence
  1035→    (∀ a : Vector Bool k,
  1036→      ndmCircuitEval cnf a = evalCNF cnf a) ∧
  1037→    -- Entropy walk determines SAT
  1038→    ((∃ a : Vector Bool k,
  1039→        (ndmEntropyWalk cnf
  1040→          (assignmentCompositePrime a)).totalEntropy = 0) ↔
  1041→      (∃ a : Vector Bool k, evalCNF cnf a = true)) ∧
  1042→    -- Prime factorization shadow
  1043→    ((∃ a : Vector Bool k, evalCNF cnf a = true) ↔
  1044→      AssignmentFreeSAT cnf) ∧
  1045→    -- All costs polynomial
  1046→    ((cnf.map (fun c => c.length)).sum ≤ cnf.length * k ∧
  1047→     ndmWalkComplexity cnf ≤ cnf.length * (k * (2 * k)) ∧
  1048→     cnfInformationContent cnf ≤
  1049→       toNat (canonical_np_poly.eval
  1050→         (ofNat (encodeCNF cnf).length))) ∧
  1051→    -- RECT bridge: a computational description exists
  1052→    (∃ prog : ComputationalDescription,
  1053→      prog.complexity ≤ cnfInformationContent cnf ∧
  1054→      programToEntropy prog ≤
  1055→        (cnfInformationContent cnf : ℝ)) := by
  1056→  refine ⟨ndmCircuitEval_eq_evalCNF cnf,
  1057→          ndmEntropyWalk_sat_iff_exists_zero cnf
  1058→            h_clauses_nonempty,
  1059→          (assignmentFree_iff_sat cnf).symm,
  1060→          ⟨ndmCircuit_cost_polynomial cnf h_clause_bound,
  1061→           ndmWalkComplexity_polynomial cnf h_clause_bound,
  1062→           information_content_le_nSquared cnf⟩,
  1063→          ?_⟩
  1064→  rcases program_entropy_inverse
  1065→    (cnfInformationContent cnf) with ⟨prog, h_entropy, h_complexity⟩
  1066→  exact ⟨prog, le_of_eq h_complexity, le_of_eq h_entropy⟩
  1067→
  1068→end InformationTheory

1→/-

     6→import InformationTheory.Complexity.CNF
     7→import InformationTheory.EntropyNumber.Basic
     8→
     9→/-!
    10→# Tableau Construction from CNF
    11→
    12→This file constructs a **Satisfying Tableau** from a CNF formula and a
    13→satisfying assignment. The tableau records a *witness path* for every
    14→clause -- the `EntropyNat` encoding of the variable index that
    15→satisfies it.
    16→
    17→## Main definitions
    18→
    19→* `PathToConstraint` -- the `EntropyNat` path cost for a single
    20→  literal.
    21→* `SatisfyingTableau` -- a CNF together with a satisfying assignment
    22→  and witness paths.
    23→* `SatisfyingTableau.complexity` -- total witness-path cost.
    24→* `walkCNFPaths` -- the noncomputable walk that builds a tableau from a
    25→  certified endpoint.
    26→* `computeTableau?` -- the computable version returning `Option`.
    27→
    28→## Main results
    29→
    30→* `path_complexity_le_k` -- each clause path costs at most `k`.
    31→* `walkComplexity_upper_bound` -- total walk cost is at most
    32→  `cnf.length * k`.
    33→* `computeTableau_none_iff_not_sat` -- `computeTableau?` returns `none`
    34→  iff the candidate does not satisfy the CNF.
    35→* `computeTableau_time_bounded` -- the computable tableau satisfies the
    36→  same upper bound.
    37→-/
    38→
    39→namespace InformationTheory
    40→
    41→/-!
    42→## Path to Constraint
    43→-/
    44→
    45→/-- The `EntropyNat` path cost to verify a single literal.
    46→Verifying the `i`-th literal in a `k`-variable system requires a
    47→computational path of complexity `i`. -/
    48→def PathToConstraint {k : ℕ} (l : Literal k) : EntropyNat :=
    49→  EntropyNat.ofNat l.particle_idx.val
    50→
    51→/-!
    52→## The Satisfying Tableau (Certificate Structure)
    53→
    54→A `SatisfyingTableau` bundles:
    55→1. `cnf`: The constraint formula.
    56→2. `assignment`: A `Vector Bool k` -- the endpoint.
    57→3. `walk_paths`: A `List EntropyNat` -- the recorded walk.
    58→   For each clause, this records the `PathToConstraint` of the literal reached.
    59→4. `h_valid`: A proof that the endpoint satisfies all constraints.
    60→
    61→The `walk_paths` field is the physical record of the walk. Its sum
    62→(`complexity`) measures the total path length -- the information cost of the
    63→certificate. This is bounded by the CNF's structure alone.
    64→-/
    65→structure SatisfyingTableau (k : ℕ) where
    66→  cnf : SyntacticCNF k
    67→  assignment : Vector Bool k
    68→  walk_paths : List EntropyNat
    69→  h_valid : evalCNF cnf assignment = true
    70→
    71→/--
    72→**Measures the complexity of a Satisfying Tableau.**
    73→
    74→The complexity is the sum of the `EntropyNat` lengths in the walk record.
    75→Each path is bijectively a natural number (`EntropyNat.toNat`), so this sum is a concrete
    76→`ℕ` -- the total information cost of the certificate.
    77→-/
    78→def SatisfyingTableau.complexity {k : ℕ} (tableau : SatisfyingTableau k) : ℕ :=
    79→  (tableau.walk_paths.map EntropyNat.toNat).sum
    80→
    81→/--
    82→**The Full Walk: Visits every clause and records the path to its satisfied literal.**
    83→
    84→Given a CNF and an endpoint (a satisfying assignment), `walkCNFPaths` walks
    85→every clause in the CNF. For each clause, it finds the first literal satisfied
    86→by the endpoint and records the `PathToConstraint` -- the distance to
    87→that literal's variable index.
    88→
    89→The walk visits |cnf| clauses. Each clause's literal index is at most k.
    90→Therefore the total walk cost is bounded by |cnf| x k, which is bounded by n^2
    91→where n = |SyntacticCNF.encode cnf|.
    92→
    93→Since `walk_paths : List EntropyNat` is `List (List Bool)` which flattens
    94→to `List Bool` = `ComputerTape` = `ComputerProgram`, the walk itself constructs
    95→the computation tape.
    96→-/
    97→def walkCNFPaths {k : ℕ} (cnf : SyntacticCNF k)
    98→    (endpoint : { v : Vector Bool k //
    99→      evalCNF cnf v = true }) :
   100→    SatisfyingTableau k :=
   101→  let assignment := endpoint.val
   102→  let h_valid := endpoint.property
   103→  -- Build the witness path for each clause.
   104→  let walk_paths := cnf.map (fun clause =>
   105→    let witness_literal_opt :=
   106→      clause.find? (fun lit => evalLiteral lit assignment)
   107→    match witness_literal_opt with
   108→    | some lit => PathToConstraint lit
   109→    | none => EntropyNat.ofNat 0
   110→  )
   111→  -- Assemble the tableau.
   112→  { cnf := cnf,
   113→    assignment := assignment,
   114→    walk_paths := walk_paths,
   115→    h_valid := h_valid }
   116→
   117→/--
   118→Flatten the witness-path trace into a `ComputerProgram`.
   119→This makes explicit that the certificate trace is an executable tape/program.
   120→-/
   121→def SatisfyingTableau.toComputerProgram {k : ℕ}
   122→    (tableau : SatisfyingTableau k) : ComputerProgram :=
   123→  List.flatten (tableau.walk_paths.map (fun p => p.val))
   124→
   125→lemma path_complexity_le_k {k : ℕ} (clause : Clause k) (endpoint : Vector Bool k) :
   126→  (EntropyNat.toNat (match clause.find? (fun lit => evalLiteral lit endpoint) with
   127→   | some lit => EntropyNat.ofNat lit.particle_idx.val
   128→   | none => EntropyNat.ofNat 0)) ≤ k := by
   129→  cases h_find : clause.find? (fun lit => evalLiteral lit endpoint) with
   130→  | none =>
   131→    simp only [EntropyNat.toNat, EntropyNat.ofNat, List.length_replicate]
   132→    exact Nat.zero_le k
   133→  | some witness_lit =>
   134→    simp only [EntropyNat.toNat, EntropyNat.ofNat, List.length_replicate]
   135→    exact Nat.le_of_lt witness_lit.particle_idx.isLt
   136→
   137→/--
   138→**The N^2 Walk Bound: Total walk cost is bounded by |cnf| x k.**
   139→
   140→The walk visits |cnf| clauses. At each clause, the farthest reachable literal
   141→has index < k. Therefore the total cost is at most |cnf| x k. Since both
   142→|cnf| <= n and k <= n (where n = |SyntacticCNF.encode cnf|, proved by
   143→`cnf_length_le_encoded_length` and `SyntacticCNF.encode_size_ge_k`), the total cost
   144→is bounded by n x n = n^2.
   145→
   146→This bound depends ONLY on the CNF's dimensions -- not on the endpoint.
   147→Any endpoint that satisfies the CNF produces a walk with cost <= |cnf| x k.
   148→-/
   149→theorem walkComplexity_upper_bound {k : ℕ}
   150→    (cnf : SyntacticCNF k)
   151→    (endpoint : { v : Vector Bool k //
   152→      evalCNF cnf v = true }) :
   153→  (walkCNFPaths cnf endpoint).complexity ≤ cnf.length * k :=
   154→by
   155→  have h_bound_element : ∀ clause ∈ cnf,
   156→    (EntropyNat.toNat (match clause.find? (fun lit => evalLiteral lit endpoint.val) with
   157→    | some lit => EntropyNat.ofNat lit.particle_idx.val
   158→    | none => EntropyNat.ofNat 0)) ≤ k := by
   159→    intro clause _
   160→    exact path_complexity_le_k clause endpoint.val
   161→  unfold walkCNFPaths SatisfyingTableau.complexity
   162→  simp [PathToConstraint, List.map_map]
   163→  induction cnf with
   164→  | nil => simp
   165→  | cons head tail ih =>
   166→    simp [List.map_cons, List.sum_cons, List.length_cons]
   167→    have h_head :
   168→        (EntropyNat.toNat (match
   169→          head.find? (fun lit =>
   170→            evalLiteral lit endpoint.val) with
   171→        | some lit => EntropyNat.ofNat lit.particle_idx.val
   172→        | none => EntropyNat.ofNat 0)) ≤ k :=
   173→      path_complexity_le_k head endpoint.val
   174→    have h_tail :
   175→        (tail.map (EntropyNat.toNat ∘ fun clause =>
   176→          match clause.find? (fun lit =>
   177→            evalLiteral lit endpoint.val) with
   178→          | some lit => EntropyNat.ofNat lit.particle_idx.val
   179→          | none =>
   180→            EntropyNat.ofNat 0)).sum ≤
   181→              tail.length * k := by
   182→      have h_tail_sat :
   183→          evalCNF tail endpoint.val = true := by
   184→        have h_full_sat := endpoint.property
   185→        unfold evalCNF at h_full_sat ⊢
   186→        rw [List.all_cons] at h_full_sat
   187→        simp only [Bool.and_eq_true] at h_full_sat
   188→        exact h_full_sat.2
   189→      let tail_endpoint :
   190→          { v : Vector Bool k //
   191→            evalCNF tail v = true } :=
   192→        ⟨endpoint.val, h_tail_sat⟩
   193→      apply ih tail_endpoint
   194→      intro clause h_mem_tail
   195→      exact path_complexity_le_k clause endpoint.val
   196→    linarith [h_head, h_tail]
   197→
   198→/--
   199→**Computable Walk (The Universal Tableau Generator).**
   200→
   201→This is the computable version of `walkCNFPaths`. It takes a CNF and a
   202→candidate endpoint (`Vector Bool k`) and returns `some SatisfyingTableau`
   203→if the candidate is valid, `none` otherwise.
   204→
   205→This function does NOT use `Exists.choose` or Classical.choice.
   206→It is purely computable -- executable Lean code.
   207→
   208→The walk logic is identical to `walkCNFPaths`: visit every clause, record the
   209→path to the satisfied literal. The only difference is that the validity check
   210→(`evalCNF cnf candidate`) is performed computationally via `if h_valid : ...`.
   211→-/
   212→def computeTableau? {k : ℕ} (cnf : SyntacticCNF k)
   213→  (candidate : Vector Bool k) : Option (SatisfyingTableau k) :=
   214→  if h_valid : evalCNF cnf candidate = true then
   215→    let walk_paths := cnf.map (fun clause =>
   216→      match clause.find? (fun lit => evalLiteral lit candidate) with
   217→      | some lit => PathToConstraint lit
   218→      | none     => EntropyNat.ofNat 0
   219→    )
   220→    some {
   221→      cnf := cnf,
   222→      assignment := candidate,
   223→      walk_paths := walk_paths,
   224→      h_valid := h_valid
   225→    }
   226→  else
   227→    none
   228→
   229→/--
   230→**Lemma: `computeTableau_none_iff_not_sat` returns `none` iff
   231→the candidate does not satisfy the CNF.**
   232→
   233→This follows directly from the `if`/`else` branch structure of `computeTableau?`.
   234→-/
   235→theorem computeTableau_none_iff_not_sat {k : ℕ} (cnf : SyntacticCNF k) (v : Vector Bool k) :
   236→    computeTableau? cnf v = none ↔ evalCNF cnf v = false := by
   237→  constructor
   238→  · intro h_none
   239→    unfold computeTableau? at h_none
   240→    by_contra h_not_false
   241→    push_neg at h_not_false
   242→    have h_true : evalCNF cnf v = true := by
   243→      cases evalCNF cnf v <;> simp_all
   244→    simp [h_true] at h_none
   245→  · intro h_false
   246→    unfold computeTableau?
   247→    simp [h_false]
   248→
   249→/--
   250→**Lemma: When `computeTableau?` returns `some`, the resulting tableau's
   251→complexity is bounded by `cnf.length * k`.**
   252→
   253→This matches the `walkComplexity_upper_bound` bound. The walk logic in
   254→`computeTableau?` constructs the same `walk_paths` structure as
   255→`walkCNFPaths`, so the same per-clause bound applies.
   256→-/
   257→theorem computeTableau_time_bounded {k : ℕ} (cnf : SyntacticCNF k) (v : Vector Bool k)
   258→    (tableau : SatisfyingTableau k)
   259→    (h : computeTableau? cnf v = some tableau) :
   260→    tableau.complexity ≤ cnf.length * k := by
   261→  -- Extract that evalCNF cnf v = true from the `some` branch
   262→  have h_valid : evalCNF cnf v = true := by
   263→    unfold computeTableau? at h
   264→    split at h
   265→    · case isTrue h_true => exact h_true
   266→    · case isFalse => simp at h
   267→  -- The tableau from computeTableau? has specific structure
   268→  have h_tableau : tableau = {
   269→      cnf := cnf,
   270→      assignment := v,
   271→      walk_paths := cnf.map (fun clause =>
   272→        match clause.find? (fun lit => evalLiteral lit v) with
   273→        | some lit => PathToConstraint lit
   274→        | none     => EntropyNat.ofNat 0),
   275→      h_valid := h_valid
   276→    } := by
   277→    unfold computeTableau? at h
   278→    simp [h_valid] at h
   279→    exact h.symm
   280→  -- The tableau equals the one produced by walkCNFPaths, so reuse its bound
   281→  let endpoint : { w : Vector Bool k // evalCNF cnf w = true } := ⟨v, h_valid⟩
   282→  have h_eq : tableau.complexity = (walkCNFPaths cnf endpoint).complexity := by
   283→    rw [h_tableau]
   284→    rfl
   285→  rw [h_eq]
   286→  exact walkComplexity_upper_bound cnf endpoint
   287→
   288→end InformationTheory
